docs.title: STRiDE
docs.text:
Microsatellite Instability prediction for MSK-ACCESS cfDNA sequencing.

STRiDE extracts repeat-frequency features from paired tumor/normal BAMs at 170 curated microsatellite loci and classifies samples as MSI-H or MSS using a trained machine learning model.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install stride-msk

# Single-sample end-to-end
stride run \
    --tumor-bam /data/tumor.bam \
    --normal-bam /data/normal.bam \
    --out-dir results/

# Batch mode
stride run \
    --samples-list samples.csv \
    --out-dir results/

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 🧬 170 curated MSI loci — validated for cfDNA panel sequencing
  • 📊 36+ features per site — statistical, distance, allele, and quality metrics
  • 🤖 Trained SGD classifier — bundled model, no setup required
  • 📋 Rich CLI — progress bars, colored tables, structured logging
  • 🐳 Docker support — ghcr.io/msk-access/stride

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text:
Research Use Only

This pipeline is intended for research use within MSK-ACCESS and has not been validated for clinical deployment. Use and interpretation of results should follow institutional guidelines.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text: STRiDE is a microsatellite instability (MSI) prediction pipeline for MSK-ACCESS cfDNA sequencing. It extracts repeat-frequency features from paired tumor/normal BAMs at 170 curated microsatellite loci, then classifies samples as MSI-H or MSS using a trained SGD classifier.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Tumor BAM] --> C[MSIProfileGenerator]
    B[Normal BAM] --> C
    D[170 MSI Sites] --> C
    C --> E[Feature TSV]
    E --> F[Predictor]
    G[Trained Model] --> F
    F --> H[MSI/MSS Prediction]

docs.title: Module Map
docs.text: Module Responsibility cli.py Typer CLI with features, predict, run sub-commands feature_generator.py BAM parsing, repeat counting, statistical feature extraction predictor.py Model loading, feature matrix assembly, scoring pipeline.py Orchestration — single/batch feature → prediction flows utils.py Logging setup (RichHandler), filename helpers, sample-list I/O models/__init__.py importlib.resources helpers for bundled model/data

docs.title: Feature Taxonomy (36+ per site)
docs.text:
Each of the 170 sites produces features in these categories:

  • Statistical: chi-squared p-value, Shannon entropy (tumor/normal/diff)
  • Distance: L1, L2, Wasserstein distance between normalized repeat distributions
  • Allele counts: allele count differences at 7 absolute thresholds (1–30) and 6 normalized thresholds (1%–6%)
  • Quality metrics: mean mapping quality, base quality (tumor/normal)
  • Insert sizes: mean insert size (all/ref-matching/alt reads, tumor/normal)
  • Coverage: raw and normalized repeat frequency distributions

docs.title: Model Architecture
docs.text:
The default model is an sklearn.Pipeline: 1. StandardScaler — feature normalization 2. SGDClassifier — stochastic gradient descent for MSI-H vs MSS

The predictor.unwrap_model() function handles multiple serialization formats (Pipeline, dict with scaler+clf, dict with pipeline key).

docs.title: Resource Management
docs.text:
• BAM files are managed via context managers (MSIProfileGenerator.__enter__/__exit__)
  • Bundled data accessed via importlib.resources.files() for cross-platform compatibility
  • Logging configured centrally by utils.setup_logging(), called once from the CLI layer

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to STRiDE are documented here.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Typer CLI with sub-commands (features, predict, run)
  • Rich logging with RichHandler and progress bars
  • Bundled default MSI model and 170-site locus list
  • pyproject.toml entry points, metadata, and dev/docs extras
  • .gitignore and CHANGELOG.md
  • Context manager support for MSIProfileGenerator (fixes BAM file handle leak)
  • QC HTML report — interactive, self-contained report (stride qc)
  • Three-tab layout: Dashboard, Site Explorer, Data Table
  • Dashboard with 8 interactive Plotly cards (waterfalls, volcano plots, distance correlation, distributions, entropy scatter, quality violins, insert-size histogram)
  • Site Explorer: searchable combobox, ‹/› navigation, raw/normalized toggle, dynamic x-axis, quality badges, per-locus stats
  • Data Table powered by Tabulator.js with frozen columns, progress-bar formatters, filters, sort, CSV export
  • Light / dark theme toggle (persists across tabs)
  • --generate-qc flag for stride run to auto-generate reports
  • Nextflow DSL2 pipeline — nf-core-compatible workflow
  • STRIDE_RUN module wrapping stride run for per-sample parallelism
  • Standalone modules: STRIDE_FEATURES, STRIDE_PREDICT, STRIDE_QC
  • Profiles: Docker, Singularity, SLURM (cmobic_cpu), local
  • Dual BAI index discovery (.bam.bai + .bai)
  • Execution reports: trace, timeline, DAG, HTML report
  • Test profile for CI validation
  • Dockerfile — add [qc] extra, OCI authors label, install verification

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Migrated from argparse scripts to Typer CLI (all options, no positional args)
  • Replaced print() statements with structured logging in predictor.py
  • Moved logging.basicConfig() from module level to CLI layer

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Initial STRiDE pipeline with MSI feature extraction and prediction
  • MSIProfileGenerator for repeat counting and statistical features
  • Batch and single-sample prediction modes
  • 170 curated MSI loci site list

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to STRiDE! Please review the guidelines below.

docs.title: Contributing to STRiDE
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to STRiDE! This document provides guidelines for contributing to the project.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/msk-access/STRiDE.git
cd STRiDE
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Git Flow
docs.text:
We follow a Git Flow branching model:

  1. Fork or clone the repository
  2. Create a feature branch from develop: git checkout -b feature/my-feature develop
  3. Make your changes
  4. Run tests: pytest tests/ -v
  5. Run linting: ruff check src/ tests/ && black --check src/ tests/
  6. Commit with a descriptive message following Conventional Commits
  7. Push and open a Pull Request against develop

docs.title: Code Standards
docs.text:
• Python: 3.9+
  • Formatting: Black (line length 100)
  • Linting: Ruff
  • Type checking: mypy
  • CLI: All parameters as typer.Option() — no positional arguments
  • Logging: Use logging.getLogger(__name__) — never print() or logging.basicConfig()
  • Resources: Access bundled files via importlib.resources — never hardcode paths
  • BAM files: Always use context managers

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
All new features and bug fixes should include tests:

# Run all tests
pytest tests/ -v

# With coverage
pytest --cov=stride --cov-report=term-missing

docs.title: Commit Messages
docs.text:
Follow Conventional Commits:

  • feat: — new feature
  • fix: — bug fix
  • docs: — documentation changes
  • chore: — maintenance tasks
  • test: — adding or updating tests
  • refactor: — code refactoring without behaviour change

docs.title: Reporting Issues
docs.text:
Use GitHub Issues to report bugs or request features. Include:

  • STRiDE version (stride --version)
  • Python version
  • Steps to reproduce
  • Expected vs actual behaviour

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text: pip install stride-msk

docs.title: Development Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/msk-access/STRiDE.git
cd STRiDE
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
# Pull from GitHub Container Registry
docker pull ghcr.io/msk-access/stride:latest

# Run
docker run --rm -v /data:/data ghcr.io/msk-access/stride \
    run --tumor-bam /data/tumor.bam --normal-bam /data/normal.bam --out-dir /data/results

# Singularity (HPC)
singularity pull docker://ghcr.io/msk-access/stride:latest
singularity exec stride_latest.sif stride --version

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python ≥ 3.9
  • pysam ≥ 0.21.0
  • scikit-learn, numpy, pandas, scipy

docs.title: Single Sample
docs.text:
Run the full pipeline on one tumor/normal BAM pair:

stride run \
    --tumor-bam /path/to/tumor.bam \
    --normal-bam /path/to/normal.bam \
    --out-dir results/ \
    --verbose

This will:

  1. Extract features from 170 MSI loci
  2. Predict MSI-H vs MSS
  3. Write prediction to results/predictions/<sample>_msi.txt

docs.title: 1. Generate Features Only
docs.text:
stride features \
    --tumor-bam tumor.bam \
    --normal-bam normal.bam \
    --out-dir features_output/

docs.title: 2. Predict from Features
docs.text:
stride predict \
    --features-dir features_output/features/ \
    --out-dir predictions/

docs.title: Custom Model or Site List
docs.text:
Override the bundled defaults:

stride run \
    --tumor-bam tumor.bam \
    --normal-bam normal.bam \
    --model-joblib /path/to/custom_model.joblib \
    --site-list /path/to/custom_sites.txt \
    --out-dir results/

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Process multiple samples in a single stride run invocation using a sample manifest.

docs.title: Sample Manifest Format
docs.text:
Create a CSV or TSV file with columns:

Column Aliases Required Description sample_id sample, id ✅ Unique sample identifier (maps to Tumor_Sample_Barcode in output) tumor_bam tumor, tumor_path ✅ Path to tumor BAM normal_bam normal, normal_path ✅ Path to normal BAM matched_norm_sample_barcode normal_barcode, normal_sample_barcode, matched_normal ❌ Explicit matched-normal barcode. Defaults to normal BAM basename

Example samples.csv:

sample_id,tumor_bam,normal_bam,matched_norm_sample_barcode
PATIENT_001,/data/P001_T.bam,/data/P001_N.bam,P001-N01-IM6
PATIENT_002,/data/P002_T.bam,/data/P002_N.bam,P002-N01-IM6
PATIENT_003,/data/P003_T.bam,/data/P003_N.bam,P003-N01-IM6

If matched_norm_sample_barcode is omitted, the normal barcode is auto-derived from the normal_bam filename:

sample_id,tumor_bam,normal_bam
PATIENT_001,/data/P001_T.bam,/data/P001_N.bam
PATIENT_002,/data/P002_T.bam,/data/P002_N.bam

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
stride run \
    --samples-list samples.csv \
    --out-dir batch_results/ \
    --verbose

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text:
batch_results/
├── features/
│   ├── msi_features_PATIENT_001.tsv
│   ├── msi_features_PATIENT_002.tsv
│   └── msi_features_PATIENT_003.tsv
└── predictions/
    ├── PATIENT_001_msi.txt
    ├── PATIENT_002_msi.txt
    └── PATIENT_003_msi.txt

Each _msi.txt prediction file contains MAF-aligned columns: Tumor_Sample_Barcode, Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode, MSI_class_predicted, msi_score.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
Remove intermediate feature TSVs after prediction:

stride run --samples-list samples.csv --out-dir results/ --delete-features

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The stride features command extracts 36+ statistical features from each of 170 curated microsatellite loci by comparing repeat-frequency distributions between tumor and normal BAMs.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
stride features \
    --tumor-bam /path/to/tumor.bam \
    --normal-bam /path/to/normal.bam \
    --out-dir output/ \
    --sample-id PATIENT_001

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Description --tumor-bam required Path to tumor BAM file --normal-bam required Path to normal BAM file --out-dir out Base output directory --site-list bundled 170-site list Custom MSI loci file --output-tsv auto-generated Explicit output TSV path --sample-id from BAM filename Sample ID for output naming --min-coverage 20 Minimum read coverage per site --max-repeat-bins 100 Maximum repeat-count bins --verbose / -V off Enable debug logging

docs.title: Feature Categories
docs.text:
• Statistical: chi-squared p-value, Shannon entropy
  • Distance: L1, L2, Wasserstein distance
  • Allele: count differences at multiple thresholds
  • Quality: mapping quality, base quality means
  • Insert size: mean insert sizes (all/ref/alt reads)

docs.title: Nextflow Pipeline
docs.text: Run STRiDE at scale on HPC or cloud using the Nextflow DSL2 pipeline.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Nextflow ≥ 23.04
  • Docker or Singularity (for containerized execution)
  • Alternatively, a local stride installation (-profile local)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
nextflow run nextflow/main.nf \
    --input samples.csv \
    --outdir results/ \
    -profile docker

docs.title: Sample Sheet
docs.text:
Use the same CSV format as batch processing:

sample_id,tumor_bam,normal_bam,matched_norm_sample_barcode
PATIENT_001,/data/P001_T.bam,/data/P001_N.bam,P001-N01-IM6
PATIENT_002,/data/P002_T.bam,/data/P002_N.bam,
Column Required Description sample_id ✅ Unique sample identifier tumor_bam ✅ Path to tumor BAM normal_bam ✅ Path to normal BAM matched_norm_sample_barcode ❌ Explicit normal barcode (defaults to BAM basename)

BAI Index Discovery

BAI files are auto-discovered. Both naming conventions are supported: sample.bam.bai and sample.bai.

docs.title: Required
docs.text: Parameter Description --input Sample sheet CSV

docs.title: Optional
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --outdir results Output directory --site_list bundled 170-site Custom MSI site list TSV --model_joblib bundled SGD model Custom trained model --min_coverage 20 Minimum read coverage per site --max_repeat_bins 100 Maximum repeat-count bins --generate_qc true Generate interactive QC HTML report --stride_version latest Container image version tag

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Select a profile with -profile <name>:

Profile Container Executor Use Case docker Docker Local Local development, CI singularity Singularity Local HPC without Docker slurm Singularity SLURM (cmobic_cpu) MSKCC HPC cluster local None Local stride installed locally test — — CI validation (minimal resources) debug — — Prints hostname before each task

Profiles can be combined:

# SLURM on MSKCC cluster
nextflow run nextflow/main.nf \
    --input samples.csv \
    --outdir results/ \
    -profile slurm

# Local development (no container)
nextflow run nextflow/main.nf \
    --input samples.csv \
    --outdir results/ \
    -profile local

# CI test
nextflow run nextflow/main.nf \
    -profile test,docker \
    --outdir test_results/

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text:
results/
├── stride/
│   ├── features/
│   │   └── msi_features_PATIENT_001.tsv
│   ├── predictions/
│   │   └── PATIENT_001_msi.txt
│   └── qc/
│       └── PATIENT_001_qc.html
└── pipeline_info/
    ├── execution_trace.txt
    ├── execution_report.html
    ├── execution_timeline.html
    └── pipeline_dag.svg

docs.title: Pipeline Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    SS["Sample Sheet CSV"] --> NF["main.nf"]
    NF --> WF["STRIDE workflow"]
    WF --> |per sample| SR["STRIDE_RUN"]
    SR --> F["features/*.tsv"]
    SR --> P["predictions/*_msi.txt"]
    SR --> Q["qc/*_qc.html"]

Each sample is processed independently and in parallel — Nextflow handles scheduling, retries, and resource management.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Module CLI Command Use Case STRIDE_RUN stride run Primary — full pipeline per sample STRIDE_FEATURES stride features Standalone feature extraction STRIDE_PREDICT stride predict Re-predict with different model STRIDE_QC stride qc Regenerate QC from existing features

docs.title: Resource Management
docs.text:
The pipeline automatically retries failed tasks on OOM/SIGKILL (exit codes 137, 143). Resources scale with retry attempts:

Module CPUs Memory Time STRIDE_RUN 2 × attempt 8 GB × attempt 2h × attempt STRIDE_FEATURES 2 × attempt 8 GB × attempt 2h × attempt STRIDE_PREDICT 1 2 GB × attempt 30m × attempt STRIDE_QC 1 2 GB × attempt 30m × attempt

Override maximum limits:

nextflow run nextflow/main.nf \
    --input samples.csv \
    --max_cpus 8 \
    --max_memory 32.GB \
    -profile slurm

docs.title: Execution Reports
docs.text:
Every run generates monitoring files in results/pipeline_info/:

File Description execution_trace.txt Per-task resource usage (CPU, memory, duration) execution_report.html Interactive HTML summary execution_timeline.html Gantt chart of task execution pipeline_dag.svg Workflow DAG visualization

docs.title: Custom Container
docs.text:
Pin a specific STRiDE version for reproducibility:

nextflow run nextflow/main.nf \
    --input samples.csv \
    --stride_version 0.1.0 \
    -profile docker

The container is pulled from ghcr.io/msk-access/stride:<version>.

docs.title: Singularity on HPC
docs.text:
For HPC environments without Docker:

# Pull and cache the container
singularity pull docker://ghcr.io/msk-access/stride:latest

# Run with Singularity profile
nextflow run nextflow/main.nf \
    --input samples.csv \
    --outdir results/ \
    -profile singularity

MSKCC Users

Use -profile slurm which automatically enables Singularity and submits to the cmobic_cpu queue.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The stride predict command loads a trained model and predicts MSI status from pre-computed feature TSVs.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
stride predict \
    --features-dir output/features/ \
    --out-dir predictions/

docs.title: Input Sources
docs.text:
You can provide feature TSVs via multiple methods:

# From a directory (recursive search for *.tsv)
stride predict --features-dir features/ --out-dir predictions/

# Explicit file list
stride predict --feature-files sample1.tsv --feature-files sample2.tsv --out-dir predictions/

# From a list file (one path per line)
stride predict --list-file feature_paths.txt --out-dir predictions/

# With matched normal barcode (MAF-standard)
stride predict --features-dir features/ --out-dir predictions/ \
    --matched-norm-sample-barcode P-0001234-N01

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Description --model-joblib bundled SGD model Custom trained model path --features-dir — Directory with feature TSVs --feature-files — One or more explicit TSV paths --list-file — File listing TSV paths --out-dir required Output directory --matched-norm-sample-barcode "" Matched normal sample barcode (MAF-standard) --verbose / -V off Enable debug logging

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Each sample produces a <tumor_barcode>_msi.txt file containing:

Column Description Tumor_Sample_Barcode Tumor sample identifier (MAF-standard) Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode Matched normal identifier (empty if not provided) MSI_class_predicted MSI = Instable, NA = Not MSI msi_score Continuous decision score

docs.title: Quality Control Reports
docs.text: STRiDE includes a powerful Quality Control (QC) module designed to help reviewers differentiate true biological Microsatellite Instability (MSI) from sequencing artifacts. Because targeted NGS panels often suffer from alignment artifacts at homopolymer edges, STRiDE generates an interactive, expert-level QC dashboard directly from the feature TSV produced during prediction.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
The QC module uses optional plotting dependencies. Install with the qc extra:

pip install "stride-msk[qc]"

This pulls in Plotly ≥ 5.15 (visualisations) and loads Tabulator.js from a CDN at runtime for the data table (no local JS build required).

docs.title: Standalone Command
docs.text:
If you already have a feature TSV (generated by stride run or stride features), you can build the QC report independently:

stride qc \
    --feature-tsv out/features/msi_features_SampleA.tsv \
    --output SampleA_qc.html

You can optionally pass the prediction result to populate the MSI label and MSI Score in the dashboard hero banner:

stride qc \
    --feature-tsv out/features/msi_features_SampleA.tsv \
    --prediction out/predictions/SampleA_msi.txt \
    --output SampleA_qc.html

docs.title: Pipeline Integration
docs.text:
Instruct stride run to automatically generate QC reports after prediction with the --generate-qc flag:

stride run \
    --samples-list batch.csv \
    --out-dir batch_run \
    --generate-qc

This creates a qc/ directory alongside features/ and predictions/ containing one HTML report per sample.

docs.title: Report Overview
docs.text: The HTML report is a single self-contained file that opens in any modern browser. It is organised into three tabs, accessed via the tab bar immediately below the Hero Banner.

docs.title: Hero Banner
docs.text:
The top-level summary strip shows:

Metric Description Prediction MSI/MSS/UNKNOWN badge (populated when --prediction is supplied) MSI Score Numeric MSI score from the prediction model Sites Total number of microsatellite loci analysed Threshold Decision threshold used by the prediction model (default 0.50) Theme Toggle 🌙/☀ button in the top-right corner; switches the entire report between dark and light mode

docs.title: Tab 1 — Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard provides a bird's-eye view of the sample's MSI landscape through eight interactive Plotly cards. All figures support pan, zoom, hover tooltips, and PNG export via the Plotly toolbar.

docs.title: 1.1 Instability Waterfalls (full-width, 1 × 3)
docs.text:
Three side-by-side waterfall (rank-ordered bar) charts for L1 Distance, L2 Distance, and Wasserstein Distance. Each panel independently ranks all loci from highest to lowest distance.

  • Interpretation: True MSI samples show a smooth, systemic rise across hundreds of loci. False positives driven by a handful of artifact-heavy sites appear as a steep cliff in just the first few bars.

docs.title: 1.2 Distance Correlation (L1 vs L2)
docs.text:
A scatter plot of L1 Distance (x) against L2 Distance (y) for every locus, coloured by Wasserstein distance. A diagonal y = x reference line is drawn.

  • Interpretation: Points far from the diagonal indicate loci where L1 and L2 disagree, often flagging distributional shifts driven by outlier bins rather than broad instability.

docs.title: 1.3 Distance Distributions
docs.text: Overlapping histograms of all three distance metrics with vertical dashed mean lines. Provides a population-level view of how the distances are distributed across all loci.

docs.title: 1.4 Volcano Plots (full-width, 1 × 3)
docs.text:
Three side-by-side volcano plots: L1, L2, and Wasserstein on the x-axis versus –log₁₀(p-value) on the y-axis. A horizontal dashed line marks the p = 0.05 significance threshold.

  • Colour coding:
  • Green dots — loci with tumour MapQ ≥ 40 (well-mapped).
  • Orange ✕ — loci with tumour MapQ < 40 (potential alignment artefact).
  • Interpretation: Genuine MSI loci cluster in the top-right (high distance, high significance). Orange crosses indicate sites where the shift may be an alignment artefact.

docs.title: 1.5 Entropy Scatter
docs.text:
Normal Entropy vs Tumour Entropy, coloured by Entropy Δ. A diagonal y = x line separates loci with entropy gain (above) from entropy loss (below).

  • Interpretation: MSI causes the repeat-length distribution to broaden → higher entropy. Loci above the diagonal with large Δ Entropy are strong MSI candidates.

docs.title: 1.6 Quality Metrics (Violins)
docs.text:
Split violin plots comparing Normal vs Tumour distributions for MapQ, Base Quality, and log₁₀(Coverage).

  • Interpretation: Ensures the two samples have comparable sequencing quality; large asymmetries could bias distance calculations.

docs.title: Tab 2 — Site Explorer
docs.text: Drill down into every individual locus with an interactive repeat-length distribution histogram. Loci are sorted by chromosome and position.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description Searchable Combobox Type to filter loci by genomic position (e.g. chr4:55); click the dropdown arrow or focus the input to browse the full list Prev / Next Navigation ‹ / › buttons with a counter (e.g. "42 / 170") for sequential browsing Raw / Normalized Toggle Pill-style buttons to swap the Y-axis between normalised frequency (0–1) and raw read counts (integers); state persists across locus changes Normal vs Tumour bars Side-by-side bars; tooltips identify Normal or Tumor and show both frequency and raw read count Dynamic X-axis Range auto-scales to the maximum observed repeat length across all sites, eliminating wasted whitespace Reference line Green dashed vertical line at the reference repeat count for the selected locus; dynamically adjusts per site Quality badge Styled badge (✓ PASS / ⚠ REVIEW / ⚠ FAIL) based on tumour MapQ and insert-size delta Stats strip L1, L2, Wass, p-value, Entropy Δ, T_Cov, N_Cov, T_MapQ, T_BQ Legend Always visible (Normal / Tumour / Ref) even when switching loci

docs.title: Tab 3 — Data Table
docs.text: A fully interactive table powered by Tabulator.js v6 with the Midnight dark theme (auto-switches with the report-wide light/dark mode toggle).

docs.title: Table Features
docs.text: Feature Description Dynamic height Table height fills the viewport (calc(100vh - 260px)) so it adapts to any screen size with vertical scrollbar Horizontal scroll Layout mode fitDataFill — columns use natural widths; a horizontal scrollbar appears when columns exceed viewport width Frozen Rank column The Rank column is frozen on the left so it remains visible during horizontal scrolling Progress bar formatters L1, L2, and Wasserstein columns display colour-gradient progress bars (green → orange) proportional to the sample-wide maximum; the exact value is overlaid as a legend Column header filters Every column has a built-in filter input in the header row (text or numeric) Click-to-sort Click any column header to sort ascending/descending Column reordering Drag column headers to rearrange Column resize Drag header borders to resize columns Header text wrapping Long header names wrap instead of truncating Conditional row styling Loci with L1 > 70% of the sample maximum get an orange left-border indicator MapQ warning Tumour MapQ values below 40 are rendered in orange bold to flag potential artefacts Tooltips Hover over L1/L2/Wass cells to see the exact numeric value Pagination Page sizes of 25 / 50 / 100 / All; defaults to 50 CSV download Click ⬇ Download CSV to export the full (filtered) table as a CSV file

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column Description Rank Rank by L1 distance (descending) Chr Chromosome Start Genomic start position Unit Repeat unit motif (e.g. A, T, AC) Count Reference repeat count L1 L1 (Manhattan) distance between normal and tumour distributions L2 L2 (Euclidean) distance Wass. Wasserstein (Earth Mover's) distance p-value KS-test p-value for distribution divergence Ent. Δ Entropy difference (tumour – normal) T_Cov Tumour total coverage at the locus N_Cov Normal total coverage at the locus T_MapQ Mean tumour mapping quality T_BQ Mean tumour base quality (if available)

docs.title: Quick Decision Flow
docs.text:
1. Check Hero Banner → known MSI/MSS or UNKNOWN?
2. Dashboard Waterfalls → systemic shift or cliff?
3. Volcano Plots → significant loci well-mapped (green) or artefactual (orange)?
4. Site Explorer → inspect top-ranked loci individually
5. Data Table → filter / search / export for reporting

docs.title: Red Flags (Potential Artefacts)
docs.text:
• 🔸 Only 1–3 loci with high distance; rest near zero (waterfalls show a cliff)
  • 🔸 High-distance loci are all orange (MapQ < 40) in the Volcano plot
  • 🔸 Large entropy delta but low coverage
  • 🔸 Tumour MapQ noticeably lower than Normal in the Quality Violins
